title: R' Nachmani

paragraphs: Hyman cites Shekalim 4:2 for R' Ila reporting in his name.

Hyman cites R' Nachmani in Midrash Tehillim 52, at the printed sublocator ד, as saying, “because he permitted,” and so on. Hyman notes that the statement appears at the beginning of Bereshit Rabbah 32 in the name of Nachman son of R' Shmuel bar Nachmani and in the Yalkut in the name of R' Nechemyah.

notes.text: Bereshit Rabbah 32:1 names Nachman, son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani. The quoted fragment “because he permitted” and the connective ע״ש in the Midrash Tehillim citation remain incompletely resolved; no verse explanation is supplied.

The earlier BereshitRabbah32:1 match naming Nachman son of Shmuel bar Nachmani is inherited, not a newly inspected whole paragraph. It supersedes the old Shimon expansion but does not settle the MidrashTehillim24 fragment שהתיר or connective ע״ש. That literal connective remains with a tentative on-account-of gloss, not an invented verse explanation or omitted object. Yalkut there remains unspecified; Nachmani, Nachman and Nechemyah remain separate attributions. Exact personal title abbreviations stay R' without new full-title evidence.

The print (vol. III, p. 946) gives Midrash Tehillim 52 with sublocator ד, where the supplied Hebrew transcription gives chapter 24. In §3 of the consulted edition, Rav Nachman explains Doeg’s epithet “the Edomite” by saying that Doeg declared that David could be killed and that David’s wife could marry another man. This supplies the context for Hyman’s abbreviated phrase ע״ש שהתיר (“because he permitted”). Section 4 recounts Doeg’s report to Saul. Bereshit Rabbah 32:1 names Nachman son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani. A parallel in Yalkut Shimoni on Samuel I (remez 131, second paragraph) names Rabbi Nechemyah son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani. Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 4:2 has Rabbi Ila reporting in the name of Shmuel bar Nachman. These are the respective readings of the consulted texts.
